back_translation: In the twenty-fifth year of our exile, at the beginning of the year, on the tenth day of the month—the fourteenth year after Jerusalem was destroyed—on that very day the hand of the LORD was upon me, and He brought me there.
In visions of God He brought me to the land of Israel and set me on a very high mountain, on whose southern side was a structure resembling a city.
He brought me there, and behold, there was a man whose appearance was like bronze, standing at the gateway, with a linen cord and a measuring rod in his hand.

The man said to me, 'Son of man, look with your eyes, hear with your ears, and pay attention to everything I am about to show you, for you have been brought here in order to see these things. Report everything you see to the house of Israel.'

And behold, there was a wall surrounding the temple area all around. The measuring rod in the man's hand was six cubits long (each cubit being a cubit and a handbreadth), and he measured the thickness of the wall to be one rod and its height one rod.
Then he came to the gate facing east, climbed its steps, and measured the threshold of the gate to be one rod deep.
Each gate chamber was one rod long and one rod wide, and there were five cubits between the gate chambers; and the inner threshold beside the gate portico facing the temple was one rod deep.
Then he measured the inner portico of the gateway; it was one rod.
He measured the gate portico to be eight cubits, and its gateposts were two cubits thick. The gate portico faced the temple.
The gate chambers of the east gate were three on each side, all three of the same measurement, and the gateposts on either side were also of the same measurement.
He measured the width of the gate entrance to be ten cubits, and the length of the gateway thirteen cubits.
In front of each gate chamber was a low wall one cubit high on each side, and each gate chamber was a square six cubits on each side.
Then he measured the gateway from the roof of one chamber to the roof of the opposite chamber; it was twenty-five cubits wide from doorway to opposite doorway.
He measured the gateposts to be sixty cubits high. The gateway extended on to the gatepost of the court.
The distance from the front of the gate entrance to the far end of the inner portico of the gate was fifty cubits.
The gate chambers and the gateposts had beveled windows all around the inside of the gateway; the porticoes also had windows all around on the inside; and on the gateposts were carved palm trees.
Then he brought me into the outer court, and behold, there were chambers and a pavement laid all around the court; thirty chambers faced the pavement.
The pavement ran beside the gateways, corresponding to the length of the gateways; this was the lower pavement.
Then he measured the distance from the front of the lower gate to the outside of the inner court—a hundred cubits, on both the east and the north sides.
He also measured the length and width of the north gateway of the outer court.
It had three gate chambers on each side, and its gateposts and portico were the same measurement as the first gate: fifty cubits long and twenty-five cubits wide.
Its windows, portico, and palm trees were the same measurement as the gate facing east; seven steps led up to it, and its portico was opposite them.
There was a gate to the inner court opposite the north gate, just as on the east; he measured from gate to gate a hundred cubits.
Then he led me toward the south, and behold, there was a gateway facing south. He measured its gateposts and portico, the same measurement as the others.
Both the gateway and its portico had windows all around, like the other windows; it was fifty cubits long and twenty-five cubits wide.
Seven steps led up to it, and its portico was opposite them; it had palm trees carved on its gateposts, one on each side.
The inner court also had a south gate; he measured from gate to gate toward the south a hundred cubits.
Then he brought me into the inner court through the south gate and measured the south gate; it had the same measurements as the others.
Its gate chambers, gateposts, and portico had the same measurements as the others; both the gateway and its portico had windows all around; it was fifty cubits long and twenty-five cubits wide.
(The porticoes around the inner court were twenty-five cubits long and five cubits deep.)
Its portico faced the outer court; its gateposts had palm trees carved on them, and eight steps led up to it.
Then he brought me into the inner court on the east side and measured the gateway; it had the same measurements as the others.
Its gate chambers, gateposts, and portico had the same measurements as the others; both the gateway and its portico had windows all around; it was fifty cubits long and twenty-five cubits wide.
Its portico faced the outer court; its gateposts had palm trees carved on each side, and eight steps led up to it.
Then he brought me to the north gate and measured it; it had the same measurements as the others.
So did its gate chambers, gateposts, and portico, and it had windows all around; it was fifty cubits long and twenty-five cubits wide.
Its portico faced the outer court; its gateposts had palm trees carved on each side, and eight steps led up to it.
There was a chamber with its entrance beside the portico of the inner gate, where the burnt offering was washed.
In the gate portico were two tables on one side and two tables on the other, for slaughtering the burnt offering, the sin offering, and the guilt offering.
Outside, as one goes up to the entrance of the north gate, were two tables, and on the other side of the gate portico were two tables.
So there were four tables on one side and four on the other beside the gate—eight tables in all—on which the sacrifices were slaughtered.

There were also four tables of dressed stone for the burnt offering, each one and a half cubits long, one and a half cubits wide, and one cubit high; on them were placed the implements used to slaughter the burnt offering and the sacrifice.
Hooks a handbreadth long were fastened all around the inside of the room, and the flesh of the offering was placed on the tables.
Outside the inner gate, within the inner court, were two chambers: one beside the north gate facing south, and another beside the south gate facing north.
The man said to me, 'This chamber facing south is for the priests who keep charge of the temple,'
'and the chamber facing north is for the priests who keep charge of the altar. These are the sons of Zadok, the only Levites who may approach the LORD to minister before Him.'
Then he measured the court; it was a square, a hundred cubits long and a hundred cubits wide, and the altar stood in front of the temple.

Then he brought me to the portico of the temple and measured the pillars of the portico to be five cubits on each side; the width of the gateway was fourteen cubits, and the sidewalls of the gate were three cubits on each side.
The portico was twenty cubits wide and eleven cubits deep, and steps led up to it; there were columns beside the gateposts, one on each side.
